subject: Infra wiring, telemetry handoff & egress plan for NovaMed Private Deployment

Subject: Initial handoff: wiring, telemetry, and egress questions for private deployment

Hi Grace / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we're ready to kick off the private deployment prep. Before we start the formal runbook, engineering needs clarity on a few items so we can align our network & security teams:

- Public egress: will outbound traffic originate from a fixed set of SNAT IPs or from ephemeral host IPs? We need this for firewall rules.
- Telemetry: what telemetry endpoints does Redwood expect to reach from the private environment (metrics, logs, tracing) and are they over HTTPS only?
- Service-to-service: any suggested port ranges for the internal control plane vs model runtime (so our infra team can reserve subnets).
- K8s vs bare-metal: NovaMed will be on a managed K8s cluster (EKS). Any agent/daemonset recommendations?

I'll attach a rough topology in a follow-up (ops@novamed will send the diagram). Can we get a checklist of exact ACL entries and a sample egress rule?

Goal: have network-prereqs and a window for validation by Dec 7.

Thanks,
Tom Reyes
Senior Cloud Engineer, NovaMed

Subject: Re: Initial handoff: wiring, telemetry, and egress questions for private deployment

Tom — thanks, this is a great starting point. Attaching a concise checklist (redwood_private_deploy_prereqs.csv) and a short sample of egress policy text that should map to your firewall rules (edge-egress-rule-sample.txt).

Quick answers up front:
- SNAT: Redwood recommends reserving a small static SNAT pool (2–4 IPs) for control-plane outbound calls. Model worker egress can be either SNATed through the same pool or use pod-level egress if you prefer per-pod IPs; we usually advise SNAT for predictable allowlists.
- Telemetry: endpoints are HTTPS-only (443). Metrics/health checks: metrics.redwood.ai:443, traces ingestion: traces.redwood.ai:443, s3-like artifact upload: us-artifacts.redwood.ai:443. We'll provide IP ranges for the control-plane as a CIDR block to add to your firewall.
- Ports: control plane (443 outbound), model runtime RPC (gRPC) default 9700–9710 (TCP), node management (SSH) only if you opt for on-prem operator. We'll include explicit ports in the CSV.
- K8s: we support a daemonset-based log/metrics agent for EKS; use hostNetwork:false (recommended), and set mtu to 1400 if you're using overlay networking.

Next steps I propose:
1) NovaMed ops to share final network diagram and CIDRs (Priya, will you send the topology?)
2) Redwood to generate SNAT-IP list and final ACLs (we'll get that to you by EOD Monday)
3) Schedule a hitless connectivity validation window (we have availability Dec 8–9)

I'll coordinate with Aditya on the MTU and kernel module notes and with Ben on the KMS/KMS bindings.

--

On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 11:45 AM Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Tom — thanks, this is a great starting point. Attaching a concise checklist...

Couple of infra-level things for the NovaMed team to confirm before we finalize the runbook:

- Subnet sizing for KV cache and model workers: recommend /24s for worker pools if you expect >200 concurrent workers, /25 is OK for small PoC.
- MTU: if you're using IPsec/VPN to our private peering, lower MTU to 1400 across the cluster to avoid fragmentation on large token payloads.
- Egress / DNS: ensure your DNS resolvers allow outbound to our telemetry hostnames and that DNS TTLs are standard (not aggressively cached).
- Kernel modules: for AVX-512 optimization paths, we don't require special modules, but if you're enabling RDMA on-prem please confirm driver versions.
- Firewall stateful timeouts: long-running streaming generation connections can last >5 minutes; please set TCP idle timeout >= 10 minutes on the firewall for the model runtime ports.

I'll add these to the runbook and include a sample iptables and an eBPF outline depending on whether NovaMed wants per-pod egress control.

-Aditya

Subject: Re: Infra wiring, telemetry handoff & egress plan for NovaMed Private Deployment — validated checklist and next steps

Thanks Priya — received the diagram and SNAT allocation. Summary and next actions below (final runbook attached to this thread):

Validation checklist (we will run these during the Dec 8 window):
- Add SNAT IPs to Redwood allowlist (Redwood action) — target EOD Dec 2.
- Firewall: open TCP 9700–9710 with 10m idle timeout; allow HTTPS to metrics.redwood.ai and traces.redwood.ai (NovaMed action).
- MTU set to 1400 on worker subnets (NovaMed action).
- Daemonset: deploy Redwood log/metrics agent with hostNetwork:false (NovaMed action).
- KMS: confirm key policy for artifact uploads; Ben to send KMS binding template (Ben action).

Attachments included in runbook: novamed_network_diagram.pdf, redwood_private_deploy_prereqs.csv, edge-egress-rule-sample.txt.

I'll circulate a link to the validation playbook in Jira (DEPLOY-83421) and book a 2-hour validation window on Dec 8 09:00–11:00 PST. Please confirm availability and call attendees (ops + security).

Thanks — excited to move this to staging.
